paper.title: Algorithm 851: CG_DESCENT, a conjugate gradient method with guaranteed descent

code.note: Fortran 77 package. Fortran/Dp/Src/src.f holds cg_descent and its routines; Fortran/Dp/Drivers/driver1.f is the User's Guide example (n = 100, starting point x = 1, grad_tol 1.d-8, default cg.parm). Compile src.f with driver1.f with gfortran and run it. The shipped Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res1 holds the printed result of that run.

claim.location: The shipped reference output Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res1 (member of 851.zip), the printed run of driver1.f: 'cg iterations: 32', 'function evaluations: 55', 'gradient evaluations: 45' for the 100-variable separable problem started at x = 1 with grad_tol 1.d-8.
claim.metric: The three integer counters the driver prints (CG iterations, function evaluations, gradient evaluations) for driver1.f, compared exactly with 32, 55 and 45 from res1.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the paper was not read in this wake.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The three values are integer counts from a deterministic algorithm, so the claim is an exact match. The function value (-653.0786727) is not claimed, because the separable minimum is available in closed form and would test nothing. A mismatch in a count is a finding to record and explain, not a reason to widen the tolerance.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one gfortran compile and one run of a 100-variable problem.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: The shipped res1 is a printed run of a nonlinear conjugate gradient code, and its iteration and evaluation counts depend on the line search, which is the method itself and is not a closed form.
